A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we successfully designed a fish robot with a soft and flexible structure, which can swim by body or caudal fin propulsion.
we developed the first fish-like robot with BCF propulsion using dielectric elastomers, which can swim at a high speed and acceleration rate, and can generate a high thrust.
we have successfully designed and fabricated a soft biomimetics fish robot that swims by body or caudal fin propulsion, and demonstrated its high potential for future applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of DEAs as actuators in soft biomimetic robots can provide a high degree of freedom in design, fabrication, operation, and control.
the design and fabrication of the soft biomimetic fish robot is a feasible and promising approach.
